evidence: dgraph_check.c:306: `if ((grafptr->flagval & DGRAPHHASEDGEGST) != 0) { /* If ghost edge array is valid */` (only place where edge loads are tested); :466: `for (edgengbnum = vertngbptr[vertglbend - vertngbmin],` with vertngbmax including the numbering hole; no range test of edgeloctax

Its sketch tested ends against [baseval, procvrttab[P]) (the global range starts at procvrttab[0], which dgraphCheck never ties to baseval) and used `continue` with cheklocval = 1 for holes (reported as 'arc data do not match'); it missed that vertloctax[v] < baseval is not checked either (now in the same test as the vendloctax checks).

fix_options.label: A: range check in the local pass, hole check in the matching rounds, unconditional load check
fix_options.summary: Local pass: vertloctax >= baseval, every end in [procvrttab[0], procvrttab[P]) ('invalid edge array'), edge loads > 0, ghost checks only under DGRAPHHASEDGEGST. Matching rounds: vertngbnnd = vertngbmin + proccnttab[procngbnum]; an end at or beyond it sets error code 4 'arc end in numbering hole'.

fix_options.tradeoffs: Stricter: graphs with non-positive edge loads, dangling ends or ends in holes are now rejected (see notes); one compare per edge in the local pass, one per matched end in the rounds (O(E) and O(E.P) already).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Follows the file's own cheklocval/goto fail structure and message style; graphCheck (sequential) already rejects out-of-range ends ('invalid edge array') so the distributed twin now matches.

fix_options.label: B: full validation in the local pass with a binary search over procvrttab
